name: Anaiah
overview: Anaiah was a male figure noted as a non-Levite leader mentioned in the book of Nehemiah. He appears specifically on the sealed document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27, highlighting his role among the leaders who committed to the covenant. His tribal affiliation is not specified in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Anaiah means 'YHWH responds,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's active involvement. This proper name is recorded in Nehemiah 10:22 and was not given by God directly but carries significant meaning within the Hebrew context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Anaiah as a descendant of Jacob, indicating his Israelite heritage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are recorded, and his tribal lineage remains unspecified.
scriptureSignificance: Anaiah's mention as a non-Levite leader who signed the covenant in Nehemiah 10:22 underscores his importance in the post-exilic community's commitment to God's law. His inclusion among the covenant binders highlights the unity of Israelite leaders beyond the Levitical tribe in upholding the renewed covenant. This positions him as a notable figure in the restoration period following the return from Babylonian exile.
